items.title: Fixed-boundary anyonic fusion-path space
items.statement_or_definition: For a complex fusion category, a simple site label a, simple boundary labels b,c, and n≥0, fix the left-associated object T_n=(((b⊗a)⊗a)…⊗a) and define H_(a,n;b,c)=Hom(c,T_n). A path is x_0=b,…,x_n=c with a retained basis index in Hom(x_j,x_(j−1)⊗a) at every vertex; no multiplicity index is suppressed.
items.strategy: Define the typed Hom space, parenthesization, split-space bases, and path labels before constructing operators.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; only finite-dimensional spaces and finite simple-object sets are used.

items.title: Fusion paths give a basis of the fixed-boundary path space
items.statement_or_definition: The path composites indexed by every admissible simple-label sequence and every split-space basis index form a basis of Hom(c,b⊗a^⊗n). Its dimension is the sum over paths of the product of the vertex fusion multiplicities.
items.strategy: Induct on n using the finite semisimple decomposition of T_(n−1)⊗a into simple summands, retaining each inclusion multiplicity.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; basis selections are finite-dimensional and finite at each fixed n.

items.strategy: Use orthogonal simple decompositions at each fusion vertex and inductively tensor the isometric inclusions.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; the proof uses only finite orthogonal direct sums.

items.title: Local anyonic channel projector
items.statement_or_definition: For adjacent copies of a simple site charge a and an allowed fusion output s, let Π_s be the projection onto the s-channel in the tree where this pair is fused first. If F_i is the typed associator change from the fixed path tree to that pair-first tree, define P_(i,s)=F_i^−1 Π_s F_i. In the unitary case, use orthonormal multiplicity bases and interpret Π_s as the orthogonal channel projection.

items.title: All-label unitary Ising normal data and ribbon coherence
items.statement:
Put $G=\mathbb Z/2=\{0,1\}$, with $0=\mathbf1$, $1=\eta$, and a third simple $D$. Use $ab=a+b$, $aD=Da=D$, and $DD=0\oplus1$, with summands ordered $(0,1)$ and every nonzero elementary fusion multiplicity equal to one. Let $d=\sqrt2$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$, $\tau=\kappa/d$, $\chi(a,b)=(-1)^{ab}$, $u(0)=1$, $u(1)=i$, and choose $\beta$ of modulus one with $\beta^2=\tau(1+i)$. There is a unitary skeletal spherical ribbon fusion category with canonical orthonormal summand vertices and the following complete normal data. All admissible one-dimensional F blocks are $1$, except $F_D^{\eta D\eta}=F_\eta^{D\eta D}=-1$, and
$$F_D^{DDD}=\frac\kappa{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Rows are right-tree channels $(f,1,1)$ and columns left-tree channels $(e,1,1)$ in the inverse-precomposition convention. Unit blocks are identities and impossible channels have the unique empty matrix. The associator permutes the $DD$ summand by addition of a group input when needed; its complete formula and pentagon are proved below.

The object braiding is $c_{a,b}=\chi(a,b)$, $c_{a,D}=c_{D,a}=u(a)$, and $c_{D,D}^g=\beta/u(g)$. The pullback R symbols are their inverses, in the specified canonical vertices. Both hexagons hold in every channel. The normalized self-duality has $\operatorname{coev}_D=\sqrt d\,i_{DD}^0$, $\operatorname{ev}_D=\kappa\sqrt d\,p_{DD}^0$, FS sign $\kappa$, positive pivotal dimension $d$, and twist $\theta_D=\kappa/\beta$; $\eta$ has dimension and FS sign one and twist $-1$. The canonical left-dual tensorator is $\kappa$ on both $DD$ channels and one on all other channels; its double-dual tensorator is one on all ten admissible channels. Relative to those duals $j_D=\kappa$, $j_0=j_\eta=1$, and $j_{a\otimes b}=\nu_{a,b}(j_a\otimes j_b)$ holds channel by channel. For explicit phase specializations write $s=e^{\pi i/8}$. These assertions construct the full category; they do not assume a sector example as a supplier.
items.strategy: Explicit full coherent normal data, root parity comparison, and cyclic F contraction; all formulas and all boundary lengths proved in the numbered proof.
items.axiom_use: Finite sums and explicitly specified orthonormal bases only.

items.title: The exact ell-four Ising gauge and parity chirality conversion
items.statement:
Set $q=e^{\pi i/4}$, $s=e^{\pi i/8}$ and $d=\sqrt2$. The specified rank-one tilting negligible quotient is ribbon-equivalent to the normal-data category of [[lem-ising-unitary-normal-data-and-ribbon-coherence]] at $\kappa=-1$, $\beta_-=-s^{-3}$, with labels $p_0=\mathbf1$, $p_1=D$, $p_2=\eta$. The full explicit normalized trivalent gauge is given in the proof using its negative-loop cup $w$, cap $b$, and $p_2=1+wb/d$. It gives $F_D^{DDD}=-2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, FS sign $-1$, positive dimension $\sqrt2$, and $\theta_D=s^3$.

Multiplying the associator by $\omega(x,y,z)=(-1)^{|x||y||z|}$ and the braiding by $(-i)^{|x||y|}$, with $D$ odd and group objects even, gives the distinct $\kappa=+1$, $\beta_+=s$ category. Flip the $D$ evaluation and keep its coevaluation. Its complete pullback R data are $R_{DD}^0=s^{-1}$, $R_{DD}^\eta=i s^{-1}$, $R_{\eta D}^D=R_{D\eta}^D=-i$, $R_{\eta\eta}^0=-1$, and unit entries one. Its twist is $\theta_D=s^{-1}$ in the actual pullback orientation. This is an associator/braiding conversion, not a vertex gauge equivalence or an unmodified positive-loop pivotal TL equivalence. Reversing its braiding and twist is a further explicitly different chirality operation.

items.title: Periodic Ising paths, two sectors, and the full line representation
items.statement:
Use either coherent $\kappa$ category of [[lem-ising-unitary-normal-data-and-ribbon-coherence]], with reference charge $D$. For $L\ge1$, a periodic path $(x_1,\ldots,x_L)$ obeys $x_iD\supset x_{i+1}$ and $x_{L+1}=x_1$, with every elementary fusion index retained. Odd $L$ gives zero space. For $L=2N$, $N\ge1$, the complete orthonormal path space is $H\oplus\bar H$, each sector of dimension $2^N$, with the explicit bit identifications in the proof. These identifications intertwine every vacuum pair projector, including wraparound:
$$P_{2j-1}|_H=(1+X_j)/2,\quad P_{2j}|_H=(1+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,$$
$$P_{2j-1}|_{\bar H}=(1+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,\quad P_{2j}|_{\bar H}=(1+X_{j+1})/2.$$
All bit indices are modulo $N$. For $N=1$ the bond is the identity; no three-distinct-site cyclic TL assertion is made for this length-two identification.

Let $C|b_1\cdots b_N\rangle=|b_2\cdots b_Nb_1\rangle$, $Q=\prod_jX_j$, and
$$K_{c,b}=2^{-N/2}(-1)^{\sum_jc_j(b_{j-1}+b_j)}.$$
The one-step periodic path shift and the annular line maps defined by the full cyclic F contraction satisfy
$$T=\begin{pmatrix}0&C\\I&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Y_\eta=\operatorname{diag}(Q,Q),\quad Y_D=\kappa^N\begin{pmatrix}0&K^\dagger\\K&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
They obey $TP_iT^{-1}=P_{i-1}$, $Y_D^2=I+Y_\eta$, $Y_\eta^2=I$, $Y_\eta Y_D=Y_DY_\eta=Y_D$, and each line map commutes with every represented $P_i$ and with $T$. In contrast the specified normalized single-chain map obeys $(K/\sqrt2)^2=(I+Q)C^{-1}/2$. The proof supplies all wrapping, kernel, rank, Hamiltonian, and intertwining assertions on the full two-sector space, without a total-flux or global-spin-parity projection.

items.title: Ising periodic paths split into two spin-chain sectors
items.statement_or_definition:
Use the actual coherent positive-FS Ising category constructed in [[lem-ising-unitary-normal-data-and-ribbon-coherence]] at $\kappa=1$, $s=e^{\pi i/8}$ and $\beta=s$. Its simple objects are $\mathbf1,\eta,D$, with $\eta^2=\mathbf1$, $\eta D=D\eta=D$ and $D^2=\mathbf1\oplus\eta$. In the inverse-pullback convention its complete data include
$$F_D^{DDD}=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\quad R_{DD}^0=s^{-1},\quad R_{DD}^\eta=i s^{-1},\quad R_{\eta D}^D=R_{D\eta}^D=-i,\quad R_{\eta\eta}^0=-1.$$
The remaining unit entries are one. Its twist is $\theta_D=s^{-1}$, positive dimension $\sqrt2$ and FS sign $+1$. This follows from the ell-four root category by the explicit associator/braiding parity conversion, rather than a vertex gauge; the original root category has negative FS and twist $s^3$.

For reference charge $D$, the full periodic path space is zero at odd length. At length $L=2N$, $N\ge1$, it is $H\oplus\bar H$, each sector of dimension $2^N$, with no total-flux or spin-parity restriction. Encode the group labels by bits, in even positions of $H$ and odd positions of $\bar H$. Under these orthonormal basis maps,
$$P_{2j-1}|_H=(I+X_j)/2,\quad P_{2j}|_H=(I+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,$$
$$P_{2j-1}|_{\bar H}=(I+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,\quad P_{2j}|_{\bar H}=(I+X_{j+1})/2.$$
Indices are cyclic modulo $N$. Put $C|b_1\cdots b_N\rangle=|b_2\cdots b_Nb_1\rangle$, $Q=\prod_jX_j$, and $K_{c,b}=2^{-N/2}(-1)^{\sum_jc_j(b_{j-1}+b_j)}$. The actual one-step shift and cyclic F-contracted line maps are
$$T=\begin{pmatrix}0&C\\I&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Y_\eta=\operatorname{diag}(Q,Q),\quad Y_D=\begin{pmatrix}0&K^\dagger\\K&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
They intertwine all displayed projectors, including wraparound; each line commutes with $T$ and the projectors, and $Y_D^2=I+Y_\eta$. The corresponding single-chain map instead satisfies $(K/\sqrt2)^2=(I+Q)C^{-1}/2$. At $N=1$ the bond projector is $I$ and the field projector is $(I+X_1)/2$; no three-distinct-site cyclic TL relation is asserted for length two.
items.strategy: Instantiate the complete coherent positive-FS category, exact parity conversion, and full periodic two-sector/line theorem.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; all path sets are finite. The category-coherence hypothesis is explicit and is not proved by the sector F/R calculation.

items.title: Fibonacci path projectors and categorical noninvertibility
items.statement_or_definition: In the coherent Fibonacci category, the three-τ total-τ path space has two channels, its vacuum-channel projectors have explicit 2×2 matrices with FS sign +1 and loop δ=φ, and [τ] is a ring unit although τ is not tensor-invertible. The identity operator on this space is invertible; this is a separate operator-level fact.
items.strategy: Use the supplied coherent F/R data, compute the two channel projections in the tree basis, and prove the ring/object/operator distinctions directly.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; all spaces and sums are finite-dimensional.

items.statement:
Use the coherent Fibonacci category and pullback-R convention of [[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-data]]. Write $\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$, $u=\phi^{-1}$, and $v=\phi^{-1/2}$. The simple fusion rule is $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$. For three tensor inputs $\tau,\tau,\tau$, comprising the incoming boundary $b=\tau$ and two sites ($n=2$), with output $c=\tau$, the path space $H_{\tau,2;\tau,\tau}$ has ordered basis $(\mathbf1,\tau)$ according to the intermediate charge. The supplied associator block is

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix}.$$

On these three tensor inputs the two adjacent vacuum-channel projectors are $P_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ and $P_2=F^{-1}P_1F$; the first pair includes the incoming boundary charge. For the literal three-site problem $n=3$, still with $b=c=\tau$, the four tensor inputs give a three-dimensional space with path basis $(x_1,x_2)=(\mathbf1,\tau),(\tau,\mathbf1),(\tau,\tau)$. The two adjacent pairs among the three sites have projectors

$$Q_1=\begin{pmatrix}u^2&0&uv\\0&0&0\\uv&0&v^2\end{pmatrix},\qquad Q_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\0&u^2&uv\\0&uv&v^2\end{pmatrix}.$$

Both are rank-one orthogonal projections and $Q_1Q_2Q_1=\phi^{-2}Q_1$; hence $\phi Q_i$ obey the adjacent Temperley–Lieb relation. Thus the two-site $2\times2$ block and the three-site $3\times3$ problem are both retained with their correct domains. The object $\tau$ is not tensor-invertible even though its fusion-ring class is a unit. The identity on this two-dimensional path space is an invertible operator; the local rank-one channel projection is not.
proof_obligations: Retain the two-site/two-dimensional block and prove the literal three-site/three-dimensional fixed-boundary Fibonacci projectors, with exact F-moves and signed TL relations.
